column8: note
Signed integer point and interval handles encode to exact half-open record keys; source handle merging, row-count hints, and all non-i64 handles remain open.
The bounded encoder accepts one physical table ID and signed handles; partition grouping, per-partition hints, and cross-partition ordering remain open.
Inclusive, exclusive, point, disjoint, and signed-extreme table-handle endpoints are exact; Datum ranges, NULL, unsigned, common-handle, and collation semantics remain open.
Only signed table-record keys are implemented; index prefixes, multi-column Datum encoding, NULL, exclusion, and collation behavior remain open.
Exact signed table key ranges can feed a request, but DAG bytes, timestamps, store type, ordering, concurrency, and the complete request envelope remain open.
The bounded leaf does not build index requests; index ranges, analyzer metadata, DAG ownership, and full request comparison remain open.
Signed handle endpoints and PrefixNext rules are exact; request hints, table/partition handle grouping, DAG metadata, and full kv.Request construction remain open.
The leaf emits exact record-key pairs only; raw key-range ownership, request defaults, paging, cache, isolation, and replica policies remain open.
Signed range encoding is bounded and deterministic; request priority, isolation, not-fill-cache, sync-log, and transactional metadata remain open.
No malformed signed interval can publish a key range; the source request validation, error matrix, and non-range fields remain open.
Multiple signed ranges preserve caller order; leader/follower/mixed replica policy, scope, concurrency, and empty-request defaults remain open.
Empty and nonempty signed range lists are distinguished; resource group, tracker, schema pointer, concurrency, and full request defaults remain open.
Signed record-key construction is independent of paging; paging enablement and paging-size byte preservation remain open.
Only bounded signed key ranges are owned here; TiKV client read-timeout metadata and propagation remain open.
Only bounded signed key ranges are owned here; maximum-execution-time conversion and request deadline behavior remain open.
Signed table ranges produce exact bytes through ordinary owned vectors; FastBuffer allocation/reuse and its full Datum range matrix remain open.
Only signed table-record ranges are implemented; FastBuffer index-range allocation and index Datum encoding remain open.
Range bytes are deterministic and carry no scheduling policy; scan-limit concurrency derivation and request publication remain open.
The leaf owns neither index lookup nor scheduling; pushed-down scan concurrency, index/table task coordination, and session variables remain open.
One physical table ID plus normalized signed-i64 endpoints encodes exactly, including exclusions and extremes; partition layouts, hints, request assembly, and unsigned handles remain open.
The API rejects expansion beyond signed integer handles by construction; common-handle tuple encoding, partition layouts, collations, and exact source vectors remain open.
Signed handle ranges preserve exact table identity and half-open boundaries; resource tags, request source, timestamps, RPC transport, and the complete handle-request envelope remain open.
